questions.stem: Consider the curve $y = 3x - x^3 - 1$ for $-3 \leq x \leq 2$. Find the stationary points and determine their nature.
options: Local maximum at \((1, 1)\); local minimum at \((-1, -3)\)
Local minimum at \((1, 1)\); local maximum at \((-1, -3)\)
Local maximum at \((1, 3)\); local minimum at \((-1, -5)\)
Local minimum at \((1, 3)\); local maximum at \((-1, -5)\)
questions.hint: Set $y' = 0$ to find stationary points. Use $y''$ to classify them.
questions.solution: The correct answer is Local maximum at \((1, 1)\); local minimum at \((-1, -3)\).

steps.explain: Step 1: Find the first derivative \(y'\) and set it equal to zero to find the \(x\)-coordinates of the stationary points.
steps.work: $$ \begin{aligned} y &= 3x - x^3 - 1 \\\\ y' &= 3 - 3x^2 \\\\ 3 - 3x^2 &= 0 \implies 3(1 - x^2) = 0 \implies x^2 = 1 \implies x = \pm 1 \end{aligned} $$

steps.explain: Step 2: Substitute \(x = 1\) and \(x = -1\) into the original function to find the corresponding \(y\)-coordinates.
steps.work: $$ \begin{aligned} \text{For } x = 1: &\quad y = 3(1) - (1)^3 - 1 = 3 - 1 - 1 = 1 \implies \text{Point at } (1, 1) \\\\ \text{For } x = -1: &\quad y = 3(-1) - (-1)^3 - 1 = -3 + 1 - 1 = -3 \implies \text{Point at } (-1, -3) \end{aligned} $$

steps.explain: Step 3: Find the second derivative \(y''\) and use it to determine the nature of each stationary point.
steps.work: $$ \begin{aligned} y'' &= -6x \\\\ \text{At } x = 1: &\quad y'' = -6(1) = -6 < 0 \implies \text{Local Maximum at } (1, 1) \\\\ \text{At } x = -1: &\quad y'' = -6(-1) = 6 > 0 \implies \text{Local Minimum at } (-1, -3) \end{aligned} $$

questions.stem: Consider the curve $y = x^3 - 3x + 2$ for $-2 \leq x \leq 3$. Find the stationary points and determine their nature.
options: Local maximum at \((-1, 4)\); local minimum at \((1, 0)\)
Local minimum at \((-1, 4)\); local maximum at \((1, 0)\)
Local maximum at \((-1, 0)\); local minimum at \((1, 4)\)
Local minimum at \((-1, 0)\); local maximum at \((1, 4)\)
questions.hint: Set $y' = 0$ to find stationary points. Use $y''$ to classify them.
questions.solution: The correct answer is Local maximum at \((-1, 4)\); local minimum at \((1, 0)\).

steps.explain: Step 1: Find the first derivative \(y'\) and set it equal to zero to find the \(x\)-coordinates of the stationary points.
Step 2: Substitute \(x = 1\) and \(x = -1\) into the original function to find the corresponding \(y\)-coordinates.
steps.work: $$ \begin{aligned} \text{For } x = 1: &\quad y = (1)^3 - 3(1) + 2 = 1 - 3 + 2 = 0 \implies \text{Point at } (1, 0) \\\\ \text{For } x = -1: &\quad y = (-1)^3 - 3(-1) + 2 = -1 + 3 + 2 = 4 \implies \text{Point at } (-1, 4) \end{aligned} $$

steps.explain: Step 3: Find the second derivative \(y''\) and use it to determine the nature of each stationary point.
steps.work: $$ \begin{aligned} y'' &= 6x \\\\ \text{At } x = 1: &\quad y'' = 6(1) = 6 > 0 \implies \text{Local Minimum at } (1, 0) \\\\ \text{At } x = -1: &\quad y'' = 6(-1) = -6 < 0 \implies \text{Local Maximum at } (-1, 4) \end{aligned} $$
